scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: The design covers the full knowledge-graph pipeline with strong temporal, retrieval, embedding, and NL-query support, but scale, worst-case latency, and schema-migration operations still need more concrete treatment.

findings.title: Capacity strategy is plausible but not yet evidenced at the full 100M+ target
findings.explanation: The graph store includes hash sharding, replication, and partition-skew monitoring, but the design does not show a concrete shard-expansion, rebalancing, or benchmark plan for growth beyond the initial shard count. That leaves the upper-end scalability posture under-specified for the stated scale.
findings.recommendation: Add a shard-expansion and rebalancing strategy, plus a scale benchmark or capacity model for growth beyond the initial shard count.

findings.title: Low-latency query path is bounded but not fully decomposed for worst-case traversals
findings.explanation: The query gateway and service enforce deadlines and traversal budgets, which is good, but the submission does not spell out how dense neighborhoods, deep traversals, or mixed query classes are kept within the 500ms target under load. The design is coherent, but the latency control strategy is incomplete.
findings.recommendation: Specify traversal pruning, caching, or precomputation tactics for expensive query patterns, and define how query classes map to latency budgets.

findings.title: Schema evolution path is not fully operationalized for live traffic
findings.explanation: The schema registry and graph update processor preserve versioned validation contracts, but the submission does not describe how incompatible ontology changes are rolled out, paused, or rolled back across active writers and readers. This is a deliverability gap for dynamic schema updates.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit schema migration playbook covering compatibility checks, staged rollout, rollback, and reader/writer version negotiation.

findings.title: Observability is strong and covers both service health and ML quality
findings.explanation: The monitoring component tracks resolution precision, relation F1, update lag, graph capacity, and query latency, which aligns closely with the operational needs of this system.

results.summary: The architecture covers the end-to-end RL trading lifecycle with versioned data, simulation, walk-forward evaluation, continuous-action policy inference, regime conditioning, pre-trade risk checks, execution, and paper-trading support.

findings.title: No material core gaps identified in the submitted architecture
findings.explanation: The design covers the full RL trading loop: historical training, simulation, continuous action inference, pre-trade risk controls, regime detection, backtesting, and paper trading, with explicit low-latency and evaluation components.

results.summary: The submission presents a coherent end-to-end ML pipeline platform with DAG orchestration, versioned definitions, cached immutable artifacts, lineage-backed replay, retries/alerts, and heterogeneous execution across CPU, GPU, and Spark.

findings.title: Immutable lineage supports replay and auditability
findings.explanation: The design records the exact source revision, dependency lock, resolved parameters, runtime identity, artifact digests, and stage attempts across the run database and tracking systems, which gives strong end-to-end lineage support.

findings.title: Content-addressed caching and storage are coherent
findings.explanation: The cache maps canonical digests to verified immutable artifacts, while feature/model stores persist checksummed objects with version references, which is a strong fit for reproducibility and deduplication.

findings.title: Asynchronous control plane keeps admission lightweight
findings.explanation: The API returns a run identifier without waiting for execution, and the orchestrator hands work to a durable queue, which is a good fit for startup latency and concurrency goals.

results.summary: Well-scoped feature store design with shared offline/online feature contracts, point-in-time joins, governed discovery, lineage, monitoring, and a coherent online serving path.

findings.title: Shared feature contract unifies training and serving
findings.explanation: The design uses one versioned feature-definition contract for both streaming and batch execution, which is the main mechanism needed to keep training and inference aligned.

findings.title: Governed catalog and lineage metadata are first-class
findings.explanation: The metadata database, discovery portal, and API together cover feature documentation, ownership, dependencies, lineage, and access requests in a coherent way.

findings.title: Monitoring spans freshness, parity, and backfill progress
findings.explanation: The monitoring component receives signals from streaming compute, batch backfill, cache, and the store, which gives operational visibility over quality and offline-online parity.

results.summary: The design covers registry versioning, artifacts, metadata, lifecycle control, approvals, lineage, and CI/CD promotion with coherent component boundaries and durable state handling.

findings.title: Model registry lifecycle, approval, lineage, and deployment flow are coherently integrated
findings.explanation: The design ties registration, immutable versioning, stage transitions, approvals, lineage storage, and CI/CD-triggered deployment into a single end-to-end path with clear ownership boundaries.

findings.title: Artifact handling is well matched to the stated 100GB constraint
findings.explanation: Multipart upload, checksum validation, scoped transfer, and immutable object versioning provide a credible path for large model artifacts without placing the bytes in the registry database.

findings.title: Transactional audit and event outbox support change traceability
findings.explanation: Registry state, approvals, audit rows, and outbox events are described as committed atomically, which is a strong fit for auditability and downstream deployment consistency.

results.summary: The design cleanly separates inference, event capture, sliding-window drift/quality evaluation, alerting, retraining, and dashboard drill-down, with strong lineage and log retention support for production model monitoring.

findings.title: Separated signal handling improves drift alert quality
findings.explanation: The evaluator distinguishes data drift, concept drift, and performance results, and the monitor evaluates them independently before triggering retraining. That separation is well matched to the brief and helps keep alert semantics clear.

findings.title: Versioned lineage is carried through serving, monitoring, and retraining
findings.explanation: Model version, feature-schema version, prediction ID, and alert provenance are preserved across the serving path, event stream, metrics store, and retraining pipeline. This creates a coherent audit trail for debugging drift and post-alert retraining.

findings.title: Dashboard drill-down is supported through filtered monitoring queries
findings.explanation: The dashboard can query by model, version, time range, cohort, feature, and signal type, and the monitoring API returns aggregate results plus drill-down references and freshness metadata. This is directly aligned with operational investigation needs.

results.summary: The design covers the full retraining lifecycle well, including trigger ingestion, validation, reproducible training, gated promotion, rollback, and lineage tracking, but it does not explicitly enforce the >1% improvement rule or the 4-hour retraining completion constraint.

findings.title: Missing explicit >1% promotion threshold
findings.explanation: The architecture compares candidates to incumbents and uses a promotion gate, but it never states the required acceptance rule that the new model must outperform the current model by more than 1%. Without that threshold, a marginal or non-improving model could be promoted contrary to the published constraint.
findings.recommendation: Add the >1% improvement threshold as an explicit policy check in the model registry/promotion gate and surface the pass/fail result in the evaluation evidence.

findings.title: No hard enforcement path for the 4-hour retraining completion target
findings.explanation: The design monitors run duration and queue age, but it does not specify an enforcement mechanism, prioritization policy, or timeout/escalation logic that ensures retraining finishes within four hours.
findings.recommendation: Define an SLA control path that measures elapsed run time, prioritizes overdue jobs, and aborts or escalates retraining runs that threaten the 4-hour limit.

findings.title: Blue-green serving provides a strong zero-downtime rollback path
findings.explanation: Retaining the incumbent while warming the candidate and atomically shifting traffic is a clear and appropriate mechanism for production release and rollback.

findings.title: Lineage tracking is explicit across the retraining cycle
findings.explanation: The catalog records run IDs, dataset and schema versions, configuration digests, gate evidence, and model lineage, which supports traceability from training inputs to promoted artifacts.

results.summary: Coherent distributed-training platform with elastic multi-node scheduling, parallel training runtime, checkpoint-based recovery, and observability for throughput and GPU utilization.

findings.title: Distributed training modes are covered in the runtime
findings.explanation: The runtime supports data, tensor, and pipeline parallelism, which directly addresses the core training-mode requirement and the large-model constraint.

findings.title: Elastic scheduling and durable queueing support large multi-node jobs
findings.explanation: The job API, durable priority queue, elastic scheduler, and GPU fleet form a coherent admission and placement path for dynamic multi-node cluster management.

findings.title: Checkpoint manifests and verified restore provide fault-tolerant recovery
findings.explanation: Checkpoint shards are written asynchronously, committed only when durable, and restored from verified manifests, which is a solid fault-tolerance pattern for training restarts.

findings.title: Input pipeline is designed to protect GPU throughput
findings.explanation: Sharded input workers, bounded prefetch, and input-wait/backlog metrics are appropriate mechanisms to avoid starvation and keep the training path fed.

results.summary: The design covers the core labeling, workflow, consensus, suggestion, export, and training integration requirements well, but it does not explicitly enforce the Kappa > 0.8 constraint as a quality gate.

findings.title: Kappa threshold is measured but not enforced as a quality gate
findings.explanation: The design reports agreement/Kappa metrics, but it does not explicitly state how the system ensures the required Kappa > 0.8 constraint is satisfied before dataset approval or export. Without a gating rule, low-agreement datasets could still be promoted if humans overlook the metric.
findings.recommendation: Add a release gate in the workflow/adjudication path that blocks approval or triggers mandatory re-adjudication when Kappa drops below 0.8, and surface that rule in the quality-monitoring feedback loop.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers REST/gRPC serving, canary and A/B routing, autoscaling, multi-framework support, batching, warm-up, and versioned monitoring with a coherent stable/candidate rollout path.

findings.title: Explicit router and isolated pools cleanly separate rollout control from inference serving
findings.explanation: The design keeps canary/A/B routing in a dedicated traffic router while stable and candidate pools remain isolated. That separation makes gradual rollout and comparisons easier to reason about and operate.

findings.title: Batching, warm-up, and readiness are combined into a coherent low-latency serving path
findings.explanation: The serving pools batch compatible requests, support warm-up/pre-loading, and expose readiness before traffic is routed. Together with latency-driven autoscaling, this is a good fit for the latency and throughput constraints.

findings.title: Version-aware monitoring supports both operations and A/B comparison
findings.explanation: Telemetry is collected per stable or candidate version and includes request logs, volume, and latency. This directly supports rollout analysis and autoscaling signals without adding unnecessary components.

results.summary: The submission presents a coherent ML data pipeline with multi-source ingestion, stage-wise validation, schema governance, dataset versioning, quality reporting, and pre-training release gating that aligns closely with the published scope.

findings.title: End-to-end quality-gated ML data pipeline is coherently assembled
findings.explanation: The design connects source ingestion, validation, versioned storage, reporting, monitoring, and training release gating in a single flow that matches the published scope.

findings.title: Schema evolution is handled with explicit policy and runtime checks
findings.explanation: Versioned contracts, compatibility rules, and validation-time checks provide a clear mechanism for absorbing schema changes without breaking downstream publication.

findings.title: Operational visibility is embedded in the pipeline rather than bolted on
findings.explanation: Stage metrics, run metrics, report storage, and alert routing are all represented, giving the design a practical observability path for quality gates and run health.
